nom: First Aid Beauty Ultra Repair Retinol Eye Cream

segments.sensitive: Reviewers with sensitive skin are the most frequent commenters, and most report the cream is gentle enough for daily use with only brief stinging or redness on first application, though a minority describe more serious burning, swelling, or a dermatologist-flagged reaction.
segments.dry: Reviewers with dry or dehydrated under-eyes report the cream leaves the area dewy and softer, with several noting it doesn't dry them out further despite containing retinol.
segments.mature: Reviewers in their 30s to 50s report smoother fine lines and less droopy or crepey skin after several weeks of consistent use, with more modest results on deeper, established wrinkles.

concerns.aging: Most reviewers report a visible softening of fine lines and crow's feet within two to four weeks of nightly use, and some describe improvement in droopiness or eyelid firmness after a couple of months; a few see no change even after extended use, and one reviewer notes it helps fine lines but not larger wrinkles.
concerns.dehydration: The cream is widely described as hydrating for dehydrated, tired-looking under-eyes, leaving skin dewy by morning; one reviewer comparing it to the discontinued original formula found the current version far less moisturizing.
concerns.redness: A small number of reviewers, several with sensitive skin, report burning, redness, swelling, or peeling strong enough to stop use — in one case on a dermatologist's advice — while others note only brief stinging or redness on first use that resolves within a day or two, and most report no redness at all.

aspects.libelle: Layers well under makeup or concealer
Pills or leaves a gritty residue
Reformulated, weaker than the original version

extraits.titre: Bring Back the Old Eye Cream PLEASE!
extraits.texte: I wanted to like the new eye cream but after 60 days I have determined it is far inferior to the previous eye cream. Not only did it burn, it was so much less moisturizing. I was surprised at how awful it made my eyes look and feel. While I have yet to find a different eye cream (the hyaluronic acid one is not moisturizing enough) for my aging eyes, I will not use this inferior product especially for the price. Please bring back the old retinol eye cream, please. First Aid Beauty is the only company that has skin care products that I love, that work and that don't irritate my skin…until this eye cream came along. I give their other products 5 stars.

[I received this product in exchange for my honest review] I've heard good things about this product. Unfortunately I had a reaction to First Aid Beauty Retinol Eye Cream. I experienced burning, redness and swelling after a couple days after using the cream. I was advised to stop using the product by my dermatologist and instructed to use a medicated ointment and antibiotics. When I first applied the cream it burned and thought it was normal until I woke up one morning with my face swelled up.

extraits.titre: Easy to use and stick with!
extraits.texte: I received the First Aid Beauty Ultra Repair Retinol Eye Cream for free from Influenster for an unbiased and honest incentivized review. This cream is stated to contain retinol, squaline, and ceramides. I actually like this cream. It's been easy to incorporate it into my daily routine. I've only used it for 3-4 weeks on most days, so I haven't noticed a difference yet. Full disclosure, I am dehydrated which shows under my eyes. This repair cream is very easy to use. It feels like it's a quality product and it goes on creamy and smoothly. It dries quickly and is hydrating. It has a really good feel and ease of application. It hasn't dried me out, broke me out, or irritated my skin. I have combination skin. It's almost scentless. I would recommend it to to see if longer use creates results.

I love all FAB products. They always work well with my very sensitive dry skin. This retinol eye cream works well for my eyes and doesn't irritate them. It also works well under makeup which I appreciate. I notice a difference in the fine lines in my under eyes when I use this consistently. I knocked a star off because I do wish it came in pump packaging instead of a squeeze tube. I think this would help preserve the product longer and dispense the right amount. Still, I recommend this eye cream! This product was gifted to me from First Aid Beauty in exchange for my honest review.

So I have very sensitive skin and the retinol alternatives I tried proved to be too harsh. On a whim I said "Hey, let's try the stuff these are supposed to take the place of," and am so happy I did. This product doesn't bother my eyes at all and after 2 months of use I can see a significant improvement to my droopy eyelid.

extraits.titre: Use morning and night* moms that need eye skin tightening
extraits.texte: [I received this product in exchange for my honest review] My new favorite cream for my under eyes. The first day I saw redness because my skin is so sensitive, but after day 2 it was completely fine. I definitely see tightening. I am 41, 3 kids deep a busy family life and I needed this! The cream itself has a scent -but it's very faint. It's a clean smell and filled into the skin great. I use morning and night.
